fact_text: The analyst says a one-year stock holding has about a 35-40% chance of losing money, falling to about 10% over five years and near zero over ten years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Investment related Questions Answered' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst cites that about 90% of traders lose money while about 90% of long-term investors do not, so a long holding horizon is a major edge.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Investment related Questions Answered' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Technical analysis is widely used abroad and is newer to Pakistan, but the analyst argues long-term stock selection rests on fundamental analysis of the business.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Investment related Questions Answered' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Of the 15 most successful market participants the analyst names, about 10 relied mainly on fundamentals, which he cites as evidence that fundamentals work.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Investment related Questions Answered' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Active trading suits only people whose own training already produces consistent results; for most investors a long-term approach is the better fit.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Investment related Questions Answered' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A stock the investor holds high conviction in can justify around 20% of a portfolio, with allocation limits kept in place rather than putting all money into one stock.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam,'Your Investment related Questions Answered' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A low price is a good entry point, but the analyst weighs each day's price against the investor's overall position rather than timing a single move.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Investment related Questions Answered' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Short-term volatility that pushes prices down is an opportunity to add to positions in businesses the investor already understands well.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Investment related Questions Answered' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Severe market crashes occur roughly once every 50-100 years in a country, so the analyst handles crash risk through diversification rather than avoiding stocks altogether.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Investment related Questions Answered' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When choosing an equity mutual fund, the analyst looks for a 10-year track record that beats the index by about 5% a year, since a strong short-term return is weak evidence.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Investment related Questions Answered' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Actively managed equity funds typically charge about 3% a year in management fees, and front-end loads add further cost, so fees must be subtracted from fund returns.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Investment related Questions Answered' (YouTube transcript, undated)
